answer: Each AI agent's identity is bound to a physical power draw signature, like timber marked before milling, so a sybil clone must replicate that metered load curve exactly. Frequency-regulation logic cross-checks each agent's claimed work against its real-time energy imbalance, flagging forged identities the way excess pigment distorts a tint, forcing attackers to rent genuine hardware per fake node. This raises sybil cost to real watts and cooling, though a well-funded adversary can still absorb that shale-like layer of capital cost at scale.
